record.paper_title: Variation Structures: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Fix n. Which simple ε-hermitian variation structures for G=Z occur as V(f) for some isolated hypersurface singularity f:(C^{n+1},0)->(C,0), where V(f) is generated by the middle homology of the Milnor fiber, intersection form, monodromy, and variation map? Give a complete characterization, taking into account known necessary restrictions such as the absence of components Wλ^{n+1-s}((-1)^{n+1}) and the condition that a Jordan block of monodromy size n+1 for eigenvalue not equal to 1 forces a Jordan block of size n for eigenvalue 1.

evidence.quote: An important element in HVϵs (Z), provided by an isolated hypersurface singularity f , is V(f ) generated by (U ; b, ρ(1), V (1)) = (middle homology of the Milnor ﬁber of f ; intersection form, monodromy, variation map).
Proposition.[11] The structures Wλn+1−s ((−1)n+1 ) do not appear in the decomposition of V(f ) for any isolated singularity f : (Cn+1 , 0) → (C, 0).

Proposition. If f : (Cn+1 , 0) → (C, 0) is an isolated singularity such that its monodromy h has a Jordan block of size n + 1 (necessarily for an eigenvalue ̸= 1), then h has a Jordan block of size n for the eigenvalue = 1.
Problem # 6. For a ﬁxed n, ﬁnd the complete set of simple variation structures (G = Z) which are given by isolated hypersurface singularities.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and ε = (−1)^n. A simple ε-hermitian variation structure over G = ℤ is an indecomposable quadruple (U; b, ρ, V), where U is a finitely generated free ℤ-module, b: U × U → ℤ is an ε-hermitian (with respect to the identity involution) bilinear form, ρ: U → U is an automorphism preserving b ("monodromy"), and V: U* → U is a "variation map" satisfying the compatibility relations of an ε-hermitian variation structure (so that b, ρ, and V determine each other in the usual way and (1 − ρ) factors through V). Up to isomorphism, the indecomposable simple ε-hermitian variation structures over ℤ are classified into families indexed by an eigenvalue λ ∈ ℂ*, a Jordan block size k ≥ 1, and an additional sign/type parameter; among these one distinguishes a family denoted W_λ^k(±1).

To any isolated hypersurface singularity f: (ℂ^{n+1}, 0) → (ℂ, 0), one associates the variation structure V(f) = (U; b, ρ, V), where U = H_n(F; ℤ) is the middle homology of the Milnor fiber F of f, b is the intersection form, ρ is the (homological) monodromy automorphism, and V is the variation map; this is a simple ε-hermitian variation structure over ℤ with ε = (−1)^n.

Two necessary conditions are known:
(a) No indecomposable summand of V(f) is isomorphic to W_λ^{n+1−s}((−1)^{n+1}) (for the relevant s);
(b) If the monodromy ρ has a Jordan block of size n+1 (which can only occur for an eigenvalue λ ≠ 1), then ρ also has a Jordan block of size n for the eigenvalue 1.

Problem: For fixed n, give a complete characterization of those simple ε-hermitian variation structures over ℤ that are realized as V(f) for some isolated hypersurface singularity f: (ℂ^{n+1}, 0) → (ℂ, 0).
artifact.status_search_result: No source was found announcing a complete characterization of the simple ε-hermitian variation structures over ℤ that arise as V(f) for isolated hypersurface singularities. Related work (e.g. Némethi's results on Seifert forms, spectral pairs, and recent Floer-theoretic studies of the variation operator) provides further necessary conditions and invariants but does not give a full classification, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Floer theory for the variation operator of an isolated singularity
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) Floer-theoretic study of the variation operator of isolated singularities; introduces new invariants but does not provide a complete realizability classification of simple variation structures.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on invariants of variation structures of isolated singularities, with no complete characterization established.

status_evidence.title: The geometric genus of hypersurface singularities — A. Némethi
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-type work by Némethi addressing invariants of isolated hypersurface singularities; the question of which variation structures are realized is mentioned as a guiding open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The realizability problem for variation structures is treated as an open guiding problem in Némethi's program.
